To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Fission track assay for Pu in bone is possible and (2) Fission track analysis of Pu in bone can be performed with a precision and accuracy that are comparable to those obtained with the most advanced analytical methods currently in use.
(1) FTA is capable of quantifying Pu concentrations in human tissue at or below 1 fCi/g, and (2) FTA is applicable to Pu in tissue from humans, animals, and plants.« less
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method of detecting and quantifying plutonium and other actinide elements in tissue samples.
the determination of the concentrations of /sup 238/U, /sup 235/U, and /sup 239,Pu in tissue samples.
the development of a fission-track assay for Pu in biological tissue.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the assay is a sensitive and reliable tool for the quantitation of Pu and U in tissue samples.
the assay has proven its validity and is ready to be applied to the analysis of human and animal specimens.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a method to detect plutonium in tissues, but it is not sensitive enough to be useful in the field.
the fission-track technique is a powerful method for the determination of Pu and U concentrations in small samples of biological tissues and bones.
we were able to develop the fundamental techniques for a fission track assay for fissile materials in tissue and to demonstrate its applicability to Pu and to some extent to U in biological samples.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fission-track assay is a viable alternative to the alpha-spectrometry method for Pu determination in human tissues and bones.
the fission track assay is capable of quantitating Pu concentrations in biological samples at a level of 10/sup -16/ Ci.
the fission track assay is a powerful tool that can be used in the future for the determination of plutonium in biological tissues and bones.
